author: Reesha
title: Jeopardy Host & Seattle Resident Ken Jennings Urges WA Voters to Defend Millionaire Tax - NewsBreak
text:
By Reesha ,
4 hours ago
TL;DR: On Thursday, when asked about some voters’ resistance to Initiative 645 during a voter rally in Yakima, Governor Bob Ferguson pointed to an unexpected Washington State millionaire ally.
Governor Bob Ferguson spoke at a Get Out the Vote Rally in Yakima on Thursday and he urges voters to vote no on Initiative 645. He mentioned to me that Jeopardy! host and Washington resident Ken Jennings says he will vote ‘No’ on Initiative 645 in the upcoming General Election , which took me by surprise.
Governor Bob Ferguson speaks at a Get Out the Vote Rally in Yakima, WA, on October 29, 2026. Photo Credit: Reesha Cosby
A Surprising Answer from Governor Ferguson on ‘Millionaire Tax’ Resistance
Governor Ferguson was the guest speaker at the United Food and Commercial Workers International Union (UFCW). The event featured speakers including local residents, Yakima City Councilmember Felisa Gonzales, and representatives from Latino Progress Alliance and Planned Parenthood Yakima Health Center. The event took place .
I was curious enough to raise my hand to ask a question during the Q&A at the end of the event. I asked the governor why he thinks so many millionaires are against the new tax on earned income over 1,000,000 dollars.
He said he’s aware that Brian Haywood, the sponsor of Initiative 645, has been vocal in his support of repealing the new tax , but hasn’t seen a lot of other resistance from the 21,000 Washington State households who would be affected by it.
Then he said that Ken Jennings and other millionaires actually support it because the taxes will be used in beneficial ways for residents of the state. Ferguson said, “He literally did a TV ad saying, ‘ Hey, I support this! ” (You can watch the ad below.)
A counter ad using AI was made against Jenning’s ad. (You can watch it below.)
Ferguson Addresses the Gateway Tax Fear
The main question that is on the minds of Washington voters is if this Millionaire tax will be a gateway to extending a tax on the rest of us who make less than a million dollars a year. Washington is one of the few states that doesn’t have a state income tax, and we like it that way!
Ferguson says that even if for some reason the Legislature passed a tax like that, he would veto it immediately because it wouldn’t be in the best interests of Washingtonians, unlike the Millionaire Tax.
Whatever your feelings are about I-645, please get out the vote before Tuesday, November 3rd at 8 p.m.
